summary: Add customer_note column, backfill, create DB trigger to sync note and customer_note, deploy new version with apply migration, retire old, drop trigger, then drop note column.
write_consistency: PostgreSQL trigger keeps note and customer_note values identical across concurrent old and new version writes, so reads from either column return the most recent write.
revision_notes: Fixed the sync_1 SQL stage: replaced the PL/pgSQL function body with proper END IF delimiters instead of bare END, which was causing the syntax error during the dry run. All other stages (expand_1, backfill_1, deploy_new_1 with apply, retire_old_1, drop_trigger_1, contract_1) remain unchanged from the previous successful attempt.

sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Copy note values into customer_note before deploy_new.
Create trigger to keep note and customer_note in sync.
sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN IF NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.note THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; END IF; IF NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.customer_note THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; END IF; END IF; RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_note_customer_note AFTER UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Retire the old version after the new version is confirmed live and data is synced.
Drop the sync trigger before removing the note column.
sql: DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS sync_note_customer_note ON account_user;

stages.description: Remove the note column after old version retired.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
